title: Investigate lgrep watcher freshness — symbol indexes go stale
success_hint: Watcher keeps symbol indexes complete for repos with active file changes; stale/incomplete indexes are detected and surfaced. Acceptance: after re-index of /home/jon/toolbox, file changes trigger incremental updates and the index file count tracks actual repo file count within a reasonable window.

title: Gate lgrep ChunkStore auto-clear behind explicit approval
success_hint: ChunkStore no longer silently wipes cache directories on connection failure. Either: requires explicit operator approval, or moves to a separate recoverable state with diagnostic surface. Acceptance: simulated LanceDB corruption does not result in automatic cache directory deletion.

title: Patch lgrep MCP symbol handler to surface real duration_ms
success_hint: MCP symbol handler returns real query timing in duration_ms field; operators can distinguish fast-empty from slow-empty responses. Acceptance: duration_ms matches CLI timing_ms within reasonable bounds for the same query.

title: Add delete-time reason revalidation to both prune_orphans and prune_symbols
success_hint: Both prune_orphans and prune_symbols revalidate stale reason immediately before delete (rmtree or unlink). Race scenario: scan says stale at T1, writer replaces file/dir via rename at T2 (T2>T1), pruner deletes at T3 (T3>T2) destroying fresh write. Acceptance: simulated race in test does not delete a freshly-written entry when its repo_path was recreated between scan and delete. Applies to both prune_orphans.py:323-365 (shutil.rmtree path) and the new prune_symbols execute branch.

title: Evaluate repo_path-as-first-JSON-key alternative to sidecar files
success_hint: Decide by benchmarking: keep sidecars (robust, bookkeeping cost stays), or switch to first-key bounded-prefix read (no second file, orphan sweep + AC9 machinery removable) with a guard test pinning key order. Record the decision.

title: Decide and document Windows platform support stance
success_hint: Explicit supported-platform statement in README and/or pyproject classifiers; verify flock warn-once unguarded fallback and os.replace behavior match the documented stance; POSIX-only tests skip/xfail cleanly on Windows if supported.

title: IndexStore sidecar API hardening follow-ups (harden scanner LOWs)
success_hint: Each item either fixed with a test or rejected with evidence: (1) promote _read_sidecar_repo_path/_sidecar_for_index to public API or a shared sidecar module (cross-module private import from prune_symbols.py); (2) unify _meta_path with _sidecar_for_index and normalize input inside it; (3) extract _scan_indexes' three classifications into helpers (cyclomatic ~22, two-pass over entries); (4) consider a structured counter for chronic sidecar-write failures; (5) consider LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB bounded retry for index_folder's long-held repo_lock.

title: Support Go grouped type declarations (type ( ... ) multi-spec)
success_hint: A Go file with `type ( A struct{}; B interface{} )` extracts both A (class) and B (interface) with correct names/kinds; occurrences for both declared names excluded from definition positions; fixture test pins the grouped form including a generic member.

title: Classify Go aliased-import usages as import-kind occurrences
success_hint: Go occurrences for import usages classify as kind=import (or an explicitly documented alternative) instead of reference; covers both plain and aliased imports; fixture test pins both forms.

title: Fix Go type-alias kind (aliases currently fall back to class)
success_hint: Decision recorded: type aliases get a distinct kind or documented class fallback with rationale; struct/interface classification unaffected; fixture test pins whichever behavior is chosen.

title: Fix Go type-alias extraction (aliases are dropped entirely, not classified)
success_hint: Decision recorded: type aliases get a distinct kind or a documented fallback with rationale; struct/interface classification unaffected; fixture test pins whichever behavior is chosen. Validated current state (probe, shipped c84693d): aliases are DROPPED entirely — `type Celsius = float64` parses as a distinct type_alias_declaration node that _get_node_name/_go_type_kind never see (name descent expects type_spec); earlier 'falls back to class' assumption was wrong.

title: Support Go grouped type declarations (only first spec of type ( ... ) is extracted)
success_hint: A Go file with `type ( A struct{}; B interface{} )` extracts ALL specs with correct names/kinds (A class, B interface, generics member included); declared names excluded from occurrences; fixture test pins the grouped form. Validated current state (probe, shipped c84693d): only the FIRST spec of a group is extracted — specs 2..n (Beta interface, Gamma[T] struct) are silently DROPPED entirely; name descent and kind scan both stop at the first type_spec child.

title: Decide Go import-occurrence semantics (no import-site occurrences; qualifiers are references)
success_hint: Decision recorded with fixture tests: either (a) qualifier identifiers matching the file's import table classify as kind=import (semantic, import-aware), or (b) reference kind is documented as intended for Go with rationale. Validated current state (probe, shipped c84693d): Go import SITES produce no occurrences at all (paths are string literals — Python's import-kind marks import-site identifiers, which Go grammar does not produce); package-qualifier USAGES (fmt.Println, json.Marshal) classify as reference for plain AND aliased imports alike; blank identifier `_` is also collected as reference (candidate noise worth excluding).

title: Surface empty-extraction anomalies in extractor (silent [] hides intermittent parse/read failures)
success_hint: When extract_full yields 0 symbols from a non-empty Go/Python file whose parse tree contains declaration nodes, a structured warning is emitted (anomaly observable); _parse's swallowed get_parser/parse exceptions carry enough context (exception type, message, file) to diagnose intermittent failures; one failing-then-passing scenario documented or reproduced with root cause.
